# Linux installation from this checkout

`tools/install-linux.sh` installs the native build dependencies, configures this
checkout, builds all installable targets, runs the unit tests through CTest and
installs Mixxx. It uses the existing Queen Mary and SoundTouch analyzers; it adds
no model, worker, Python-inference requirement or model download.

Automatic package installation supports Debian 13 or newer and Ubuntu 24.04 or
newer. Derivatives need compatible package names and configured Debian/Ubuntu
repositories. Other Linux distributions can prepare their native prerequisites
using their distribution's documentation or the existing platform build helpers,
then run this installer with `--no-deps`. Automatic dependency installation on
those distributions is not claimed. The script does not add third-party package
repositories or enable non-free repositories.

The current application requires hidapi 0.14 or newer for HID controller support.
Debian 12's standard hidapi package is too old; prepare upgraded native packages
and use `--no-deps` there instead of silently disabling controller support.

## Default installation

From an existing source checkout:

```sh
bash tools/install-linux.sh --dry-run
sudo -v
bash tools/install-linux.sh
```

The script uses noninteractive `sudo` only for native packages or a prefix that
the current user cannot write. Run `sudo -v` yourself beforehand if your account
needs a password, or run the package stage as an administrator. An expired or
unavailable sudo authorization causes a clear failure; the script does not
prompt for passwords. Existing proxy environment settings are preserved for
package operations; configured TLS and package-signature verification stay
enabled.

The defaults are:

- Install prefix: `$HOME/.local`.
- Build directory: `build-linux` in this checkout, already ignored by Git.
- Parallelism: available CPUs, capped at four jobs and reduced when the available
  memory or cgroup memory limit provides less than approximately 2 GiB per job.
- Qt 6 and QML enabled; `RelWithDebInfo` build; unit tests enabled.
- Separate CTest processes, offscreen Qt by default, and installation only after
  the checks succeed.

The default prefix does not require a system-wide installation. Launch Mixxx
directly with `$HOME/.local/bin/mixxx`, or include `$HOME/.local/bin` in your
shell's `PATH`. The installer does not edit shell startup files.

## Existing development environment

Reuse prepared packages and a compatible CMake build directory:

```sh
bash tools/install-linux.sh --no-deps \
  --build-dir build --prefix "$HOME/.local" --jobs 4
```

An existing build directory keeps its generator. A cache belonging to another
source checkout is rejected. A new build uses Ninja when it is available,
otherwise CMake selects the installed default generator. Builds and tests run as
the current user; use `--no-deps` when administrator privileges are unavailable
and the native dependencies are already installed.

Changing the install prefix may require rebuilding targets because Mixxx embeds
installation paths in generated configuration. The build directory and
`install_manifest.txt` are retained. Re-running the command refreshes dependencies
and incrementally rebuilds/reinstalls into the selected prefix; source files and
dependency declarations are not rewritten.

## Options

```text
--prefix PATH       Installation prefix; relative to the caller's directory
--build-dir PATH    Build directory; relative to the caller's directory
--jobs N            Explicit parallelism, from 1 to 256 jobs
--no-deps           Reuse native packages; skip package-manager operations
--no-tests          Disable building and running unit tests
--dry-run           Print commands without creating directories or running them
--help              Show usage
```

Paths containing spaces are supported. Keep them quoted when invoking the script.
`--no-tests` is an explicit opt-out; it does not establish that the installation
passed tests. A normal test run fails if it discovers zero tests. Upstream-disabled
test cases remain disabled and are reported by CTest.

## Scope and failure handling

The package list follows `tools/debian_buildenv.sh` for native runtime/build
libraries and Qt/QML modules, without packaging/release-only tools. Package-name
aliases are selected for Qt shader tools and Qt 5 compatibility modules. Optional
Ubuntu fonts are installed only when present in the configured repositories;
otherwise Open Sans and existing system font fallbacks remain available. The
script does not call the original helper's interactive font prompt. An existing
JACK2 installation selects its matching development package.

Dependency installation, CMake configuration, build, CTest and installation each
stop on failure and preserve the underlying command's nonzero exit status. A
failed build or test cannot fall through into installation. The final installed
binary is checked with `mixxx --version` using offscreen Qt. These checks do not
verify physical audio devices, MIDI/USB permissions or real DJ operation.

The script does not download the manual or change active udev rules. If your user
needs USB controller access and the distribution has not supplied Mixxx's udev
rule, an administrator can install the existing
`res/linux/mixxx-usb-uaccess.rules` according to the distribution's udev policy.
This is independent of the application prefix. CMake may fetch its normal,
checksum-verified native libraries such as libkeyfinder/libdjinterop when system
versions are absent; these are existing project dependencies.

Installer control-flow tests use temporary fake tools and perform no package
installation:

```sh
python3 -m unittest tools/test_install_linux.py -v
```
